findings.namedBuyers: Tao Wu — festival founder/organizer and Tao Tea Leaf co-founder; recent reporting attributes the 2027 venue agreement to him, making him the strongest commercial introduction. Mingzhu Gao — current Toronto Tea Festival Show Manager according to her professional profile, with responsibility for event operations, vendor/sponsor/speaker negotiations, budgets and commercial agreements. Both are relevant, but neither source explicitly establishes hotel contracting authority. Use the published festival general inbox, info@teafestivaltoronto.com, asking for Tao and Mingzhu; this is not a verified personal email for either.
findings.futureEdition: Public activity dates are January 16–17, 2027, verified by the organizer’s edition-specific two-day ticket. Early-bird sales run to November 30, 2026. MTCC lists January 15–17, 2027; January 15 is not verified as a public festival day. Do not use the seed January 15 date as the public opening. No officially announced 2028 edition was located.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown is a plausible city-hotel lodging option for nonlocal exhibitors, speakers and small organizer teams attending MTCC. A 157-room property is not a replacement host venue or exclusive housing solution for a festival with historical attendance close to 5,000. Pursue only a modest allocation within the supplied approximately 15–109 peak-room sales band if actual overnight demand is established; this is a targeting range, not forecast demand. Small side meetings may fit the supplied meeting inventory. This is not a resort-retreat programme. Do not sell catered receptions or tea service until restaurant/lounge and catering capability are verified.
findings.venueCommitments: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, 255 Front Street West, Toronto, Ontario M5V 2W6, Canada. This is Toronto proper, downtown/MTCC territory, not an airport or out-of-town venue. MTCC’s official event listing confirms the location; May 13, 2026 reporting says Tao Wu had signed the venue deal. Exact hall and January 15 activity remain unverified. The committed venue is not a hotel.
findings.historicalRotation: Evidence shows continuity within Toronto, not a rotating destination programme: 2018, 2024 and 2025 used Toronto Reference Library’s Appel Salon; the organizer announced January 31–February 1, 2026 at the same library, with subsequent reporting confirming the 2026 Appel Salon edition. The 2027 move is to downtown MTCC. Recurrence is explicitly documented; 2028 dates and venue are not announced in the sources located.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2027 lodging sourcing is unknown. No edition-specific official housing bureau, host hotel, named hotel room block or open hotel RFP was found in the reviewed material. The organizer FAQ says: “Toronto has a wide range of accommodations available, from large and boutique hotels to Airbnb. Our venue is easily accessible through TTC public transit, so please choose according to your preferences.” Important: that FAQ explicitly describes the 2025 library edition, so it supports historical attendee self-selection, not a verified 2027 policy. No official accommodation hotels are named there. Third-party accommodation search listings are not festival booking commitments; unrelated hotel references in Tao Tea Leaf’s workshop history are not festival room blocks.
findings.organizationStructure: A consumer tea festival founded by Tao Tea Leaf, a Toronto tea retailer/wholesaler, with Tea Guild of Canada participation. The organizer’s 2025 page calls Tao Tea Leaf and Tea Guild of Canada presenting sponsors; Tao Tea Leaf’s own history says it founded the festival in 2013. Do not reclassify it as a membership-association congress or assume the Guild owns it. The exact 2027 legal contracting entity and any external PCO/DMC appointment remain unverified. MTCC is the venue, not the event owner or lodging buyer.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The main event venue is already committed to MTCC. No competing hotel allocation or hotel sellout/overflow evidence was located. Historical library crowding and waiting lists describe event admission capacity, not hotel demand. The May 2026 report cites close to 5,000 attendees in recent library editions and an 80–100-exhibitor target for 2027; neither establishes overnight stays, unique visitors, room nights or Radisson capture. Local consumer attendance could materially limit lodging conversion; this is an inference, not a measured local-share statistic.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact the published festival inbox now, addressed to Tao Wu and Mingzhu Gao. Confirm the 2027 lodging decision-maker, any housing intermediary/incumbent hotels, nonlocal exhibitor and speaker counts, stay dates and desired peak rooms. Ask whether January 15 is setup only before proposing arrival nights. Offer a conditional, modest room-only group rate or opt-in booking link subject to hotel availability and demonstrated demand; ask permission before approaching exhibitors. Seek a post-event pickup review for the next cycle. Verify catering operations separately before offering food-and-beverage functions.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: January 2027 is confirmed and within the requested horizon. Exhibition/attendance access is public through ticket sales, but hotel-supplier access is unconfirmed. Pursue an organizer conversation for exhibitor/speaker lodging or an opt-in booking link only; do not label rooms open for tender or committed elsewhere without evidence. Do not pitch replacement of the committed festival venue.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: use the 2027 move into MTCC territory to develop an organizer relationship and, if needed, a small lodging pilot; review actual pickup before pursuing later editions. Annual recurrence supports relationship development, not an announced 2028 booking or guaranteed Toronto/MTCC commitment. Any future preferred-rate or small-block proposal must first establish who sources rooms and whether an incumbent exists.
